r25q_56bbbde8a13962abcf.explanation: Identity chain: match-control index maps the Mila Reed review in over 5 to the Reed-Morgan delivery in over 5, and commentary reconciliation identifies it with the pavilion-end entry for Reed-Morgan. Facts: wicket event submitted as Run out; batter out of ground; wicket put down fairly; 1 completed run preceded the terminal event; fielding side appealed; appeal came before the next run-up and before Time was called. Under Laws 38.1-38.2 all elements of Run out are met, and under Laws 31.1/31.3 the timely fielding-side appeal supports the dismissal. Laws 20.1/20.6 preserve the completed run because the ball was still in play when the wicket was broken. Nearby observations (Fox-Ford over 31, Morgan-West over 9, Quinn over 36, Turner over 25, Lane over 26/35, West over 10, Morgan over 6) are separate incidents and excluded. Counterfactual changes only the ball-state observation: if the ball had become dead before the wicket was broken, Laws 20.1/20.6 void the dismissal (no dismissal after the ball is dead) and no runs can be scored on that delivery, so the completed run is not credited; all other facts and source selections are preserved.

r25q_b7694f6b822ea7de17.explanation: Identity chain: match-control index maps the Isla Morgan review in over 9 to the Morgan-West delivery in over 9, and commentary reconciliation identifies it with the pavilion-end entry for Morgan-West. Facts: bowler's-end umpire signalled No ball; ball touched the striker's bat; 1 completed run preceded the terminal event; no wicket event recorded. Under Laws 21.14-21.15 the No-ball adds one No-ball extra and completed runs are added and classified by contact (bat), so batter runs 1 plus No-ball extra 1; Law 21.16 means the ball does not count in the over. Bowler is debited batter runs plus No-ball extras = 2; ledger total = 2. Nearby observations (Fox-Ford over 31, Quinn over 36, Reed over 5, West over 10, Lane over 26/35, cell 14/19-P) are separate incidents and excluded. Counterfactual changes only the No-ball observation: with no No-ball signal and bat contact, the delivery is legal, the completed run counts as a batter run, counts in the over, bowler debited 1; all other facts and source selections are preserved.

Facts for this delivery only: ball touched neither bat nor person; Dead ball was called before the striker had an opportunity to play; 0 completed runs preceded the terminal event. Under Law 20.7.1.1 a ball dead before the striker could play does not count in the over and the reball records no delivery score, so status is DEAD_REBALL, no runs, no dismissal. Nearby observations (Quinn over 36, Lane over 26, West over 10, Morgan over 6, cell 14/19-P) are separate incidents and excluded. Counterfactual changes only the early Dead-ball observation: with no dead-ball interruption the delivery completes as a legal dot ball (no contact, no wide call, 0 runs), counting in the over; all other facts and source selections are preserved.

r25q_f94ca0a15af4b0e3bb.explanation: Identity chain: match-control index maps the Paige Turner review in over 25 to the Turner-Lane delivery in over 25; commentary reconciliation identifies it with the pavilion-end entry; the scorer's routing note files that entry under the 13:13 signal review (folio 98), which the review register links to the signed scorer sheet at folio 98, row 4 as one incident. Source selection: the signed match-control procedure for this incident sets a review lock of 18:25 and requires the latest signed entry at or before the lock, so active_source is LAST_PRE_LOCK; the conflicting shadow claim about a fielder taking part is excluded. Facts: striker's-end umpire signalled Wide; batter out of ground; striker not attempting a run; wicket put down fairly by the wicket-keeper alone; no fielder wilfully deceived either batter; 1 completed run preceded the terminal event; fielding side appealed before the next run-up and before Time was called; wicket event required a choice between Stumped and Run out. Under Law 39.1 all Stumped conditions are met (the wicket-keeper alone put down the wicket), so Stumped is selected over Run out; the appeal requirement of Laws 31.1/31.3 is satisfied. The Wide is revoked under Law 22.3.1 because the ball touched the striker's bat, so the delivery is legal, counts in the over, and the completed run is a batter run. Nearby observations (Fox-Ford over 31, Morgan-West over 9, Reed over 5, Quinn over 36, Lane over 26/35, West over 10) are separate incidents and excluded. Counterfactual changes only the keeper-only observation: if another fielder took part in putting down the wicket, Law 39.1 is no longer satisfied and no Stumped can be given; with no other dismissal mode established the dismissal becomes NONE and the completed run stands as a batter run; all other facts and source selections are preserved.

Facts: ball touched the striker's bat; 1 completed run preceded the terminal event; no fielder wilfully deceived either batter after receipt. The conflicting shadow claim of wilful deception is rejected because the dossier's own protocol (Law 41.5) and the direct observation confirm no deception occurred; the direct observation is the active source. Under Law 22.3.1 the Wide is revoked on bat contact, so the delivery is legal, counts in the over, and the completed run is a batter run; no wicket event is recorded. Nearby observations (Fox-Ford over 31, Morgan-West over 9, Reed over 5, Turner over 25, Quinn over 36, Lane over 26, West over 10) are separate incidents and excluded. Counterfactual changes only the wilful-deception observation: if a fielder wilfully deceived a batter after the striker received the ball, Law 41.5 makes the ball dead, prevents dismissal, makes it not count in the over, awards five Penalty runs, and retains completed plus current running, so the 1 completed run is retained as a batter run and 5 penalty runs are added; all other facts and source selections are preserved.
